summary: Full backend + frontend regression on Phase 5 AI Doubt Solver. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_ai_doubt.py with 14 pytest cases covering thread create (with/without initial, default subject, title derivation), list ordering, detail (image redaction + has_image preservation), non-streaming send (text, multi-turn context, image, 400 on empty), SSE streaming endpoint (content-type, >=3 delta chunks, done event, persistence), delete (cascade + 404), and cross-user isolation. All 14 pass in ~28s. Frontend (mobile viewport 390x844): login -> /ai-doubt lists 4 existing threads correctly with subject icons/pills/timestamps/msg-counts; tapping the 'Reasoning' subject chip creates a new thread and navigates to chat; sending 'What is 15% of 200?' streams a live Claude Sonnet 4.6 reply with proper markdown rendering (headings, bullets, **bold**, 'Final Answer: 30', 'Shortcut / Tip' section); user 'Y' avatar and robot avatar both render; back navigation returns to list. Streaming (SSE) verified end-to-end via httpx client and via UI. One minor UX polish issue: thread title stays 'New doubt' when the first message is sent via /messages instead of at thread creation.

minor.issue: When a thread is created empty (via subject-chip tap) and the FIRST message is later sent via /messages, the thread.title is never updated from its default 'New doubt' to reflect the actual question. Cosmetic — the list card shows 'New doubt' with a preview of the AI reply as last_message, which is confusing next to sibling cards that DO carry a real title. Suggest: in send_message, if thread.message_count == 0 at entry, set title from the incoming user text (same helper as create_thread already uses).

SSE streaming route is exposed as a plain GET with the message in the query string and JWT in the Authorization header. Works, but (a) the raw prompt is visible in access logs, and (b) if EMERGENT_LLM_KEY is missing the endpoint still returns 200 and yields the config-error line as a delta — consider returning 503 instead.
list endpoint hard-caps limit to 50 by default and uses caller-supplied `limit` without upper bound clamp (could pass ?limit=100000). Minor DoS surface — clamp to e.g. min(limit, 100).

ui_bugs.issue: Card title 'New doubt' persists after the user has actually sent a question (see backend note above). Titles should be updated post-first-message for a clean list UX.

issues: Trash icon in header has no testID — for automated e2e tests recommend adding testID='aid-chat-delete' to the delete Pressable (line ~244). Also user avatar (Y) & assistant avatar have no testIDs; suggest testID='aid-msg-{role}-{index}'.

The MarkdownText renderer does not support blockquote lines starting with '> ' — the Claude reply used '> ...' in the Shortcut/Tip block and it rendered as literal '> ' prefix in plain body text (visible in screenshot). Consider treating leading '> ' as a styled blockquote or stripping it.

attachBar preview + inputBar together consume ~120px at the bottom; with keyboard open on small phones (iPhone SE) this may cover the last chat bubble. KeyboardAvoidingView is set for iOS only — Android will need a manual offset or set behavior='height'.

react_native_issues.issue: Pre-existing RN-Web warning `props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents` — still surfaces on /ai-doubt too. Not introduced by Phase 5.

action_items: (UX) In ai_doubt.send_message, when the current thread has message_count == 0, derive & update thread.title from the incoming user text (mirroring create_thread). Prevents 'New doubt' from lingering.

(A11y/testability) Add testIDs to the chat header delete Pressable (`aid-chat-delete`), the attach preview close button, and each message row (`aid-msg-{role}-{i}`) so automated e2e can exercise the destructive flow deterministically.
(Markdown) Extend MarkdownText in /app/frontend/app/ai-doubt/[tid].tsx to handle blockquote (`> `) lines — Claude regularly emits them for tips.
(Security polish) Return 503 instead of 200-with-error-delta when EMERGENT_LLM_KEY is missing; and clamp `limit` on GET /api/ai-doubt/threads to a max of e.g. 100.
(Optional) Consider hitting the stream endpoint via POST with body instead of GET+query so long prompts / images don't blow the URL length budget or leak into access logs.
critical_code_review_comments: ai_doubt.py: multi-turn context is emulated by manually prepending the last 10 turns as plain text (`Previous conversation:\n...`) rather than passing them as real chat turns. It works but doubles token usage on every send and defeats the LlmChat.session_id-based history. Consider populating chat via a per-session cache keyed on thread.id, or send the last N as UserMessage/AssistantMessage entries.

ai_doubt._ai_reply falls back to `f"AI error: {e}"` and persists that as the assistant message — meaning transient upstream failures become permanent DB rows. Prefer NOT persisting on error and returning a 502 to the client so the frontend can retry.

The SSE `gen()` handler catches Exception once but still proceeds to persist the collected (possibly empty) reply — this yields a phantom `assistant_message` with 'Sorry, I could not process that.' content and bumps message_count by 2 even when the model errored before emitting a single delta. Consider skipping persistence if `collected` is empty.

image_base64 payloads are stored on ai_messages docs (not just used transiently). For a mid-size (200KB) student photo × many threads this bloats the collection and, more importantly, gets returned in `send_message` responses (only later redacted on GET). Consider persisting to GridFS or S3 and storing only a URL.

Router uses `body: dict` instead of Pydantic models — no validation of subject enum, no length caps on `message`, no size cap on image_base64. Add a `CreateThreadIn` / `SendMessageIn` BaseModel with maxLength/validators.
MongoDB ObjectId hygiene is correct — projections `{'_id': 0}` and `_clean()` helper used everywhere. Good.
Cross-user isolation is enforced correctly via `_get_thread(tid, user_id)` filtering on both fields. 404 for foreign threads is correct behavior (avoids revealing existence).
The `_title_from` helper is `async` but does no I/O — could be sync. Minor.
ai_doubt.py at 380 lines is fine. server.py has grown to ~490 lines with all wiring — still OK but approaching the 700-line split threshold.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of critical flows verified (list, subject-chip create, streaming send, markdown render, back nav, avatars). Delete-alert UI flow not verified because RN Alert.alert renders as an in-app Modal (not a browser dialog) — API-level delete already covered by backend test.

seed_data_creation: None. Registered a temporary secondary user (qa+aid+<uuid>@avision.in) for cross-user isolation tests — thread objects are self-cleaned inside the tests via DELETE. Existing test@avision.com / Test@123 was used for all other tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: 1) Login POST returns `access_token` (not `token`) — use `j.get('access_token')`. 2) /api/auth/register REQUIRES a `phone` field (422 without it). 3) pytest.ini forces `-n 2 --dist loadscope`; for AI Doubt tests you MUST run with `-n 0` because they share a module-scoped token and per-thread state. 4) Emergent LLM key is live and Claude Sonnet 4.6 responds in ~4-8s for short quant questions and ~10-15s for image OCR — set httpx timeouts accordingly (I used 60-120s). 5) Stream endpoint returns `data: {"done": true, "message_id": "..."}\n\n` as the terminal frame; message_id matches the persisted assistant doc. 6) Image bytes are echoed back in POST /messages response (user_message.image_base64 is redacted) but ARE stored server-side; GET /threads/{tid} strips them. 7) The frontend token in localStorage key is not `avision_token` — check `/app/frontend/src/tokenStore.ts` if you need direct fetch from the browser context. 8) MarkdownText does not render blockquote lines — see design_issues.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no functional bugs. All API contracts and streaming semantics behave exactly as specified. Minor UX / hardening notes captured in action_items.
